correctness.rationale: By induction each updated relation is the original reflexive equivalence relation restricted to a common target set. The fixed formula holds precisely when both unique opposite-p colored partners survive. Two colored involutive matchings decompose into alternating paths or cycles. Endpoints peel two per round and cycles persist, proving the exact ceil(path length/2) identity. Every deleted target has a previously extant reflexive self-arrow, so this count equals the true first stationary model stage. Alternating-pair path models attain the bound for all n. A standalone checker independently evaluated 393042 models of size at most six and an n<=40 sharp family; no extrapolation from finite checks used.

value.rationale: The theorem provides a complete and sharp infinite-family classification in the smallest nontrivial two-agent S5 information-cell class. It identifies exact numbers of repeated arrow-deleting updates for any finite input, distinguishes persistent cyclic components from eroding paths, and proves unbounded transients with just one propositional bit and depth-one formula, while zero-bit and purely propositional cases stabilize in one step. The structural boundary is motivated by the paper’s exploration of repeated announcements and not merely an arbitrary finite enumeration.
